items.note: Association named, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891 (story 1).
Article VII quoted: paid by pounds of butterfat by test, not weight of cans, and the station's test governs.
"Under payment by weight nothing that followed would have cost any man a dollar."

List item, no REQUIRED line, so core fact only: Loomis (Notes, minute-book transcription), Teague (wrote the ledger line), Sill (came to the churn 1893) all appear in Section A. Roles implied, dates 1901/1905 absent.
Section A never says Selby Vose was Gideon's son nor that he was manager from 1913; both bolded elements absent. Stated only in B3 and E19, which cannot travel into A.

Station-gain line named, 1898 entry quoted verbatim with five and a quarter percent carried to the general account. (Run dates the account's start to 1897, but the line's existence, shape and 1898 entry are right.)
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Story 3 gives weighing at intake, composite sample per patron over ten days, fixed charge from the pipette, fat read as percent off the ruled neck.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice reproduced line by line, 6 doz. pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
The flat monthly shortfall (same 0.19 in June flush and February feeding, every one of 26 years) is nowhere in Section A; 0.19 does not appear in Section A at all. Stated only in D2/F1.
"They checked everything in that building except the pipette - and no burette existed on the circuit to check it with until 1921."
Born 1861, tester twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925 (story 7).
Five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat, one hand throughout, corrections crossed and initialed, never written over.
3.80 for 1896 (story 1) and the summary leaf's 3.61 within three hundredths every year since (story 5); both figures inside Section A.
8 May breakage, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61, question mark set against it.
Married Orra Brant; Emmet her brother and the biggest patron; "married into the family that had more to lose by that station than any other."

1919 circular is there, but the second bolded element - his 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as he was taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are - is not in Section A (only "Keddie gave nine sentences standing"). Given in F6, which cannot travel into A.
Died February 1934; test book to the Ordell County Historical Rooms in 1959.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom, the wet bottom, Emmet Brant's the biggest.
The two scales agreeing is stated ("never fell out in thirty years"), but the bolded start date 1 January 1897 is absent from Section A (it appears only in E15).
Complaints from 1902 that Ostrey Hollow milk did not test with the rest. No conflation of the visible gap with 0.19 anywhere in the sheet.
Grigg's 1908 committee, January-February-March sampling, wet-hay finding reported as their finding and treated as the wrong answer.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportionality of the loss appear only in C2 and D2, never in Section A.
Custody chain absent from Section A: no passage to Roy Brant in 1929 and no loan to Ivy in 1958. Only the 1962/1963 disposal is given.
Redlow Ridge is never named anywhere in the sheet, and the Alder Corners Cheese Company is not named as such in Section A; the key gates this item on company, ridge, county and Cudd together.
Four Hessel Bottom men, summer milk, from 1915.

REQUIRED met: framed as one of four independent disproofs, with the uncompared book ("never thought to compare... not keeping a check on another man's arithmetic") plus the named artifact (the Alder Corners figures / Rosalie Cudd's table).
Same four men's milk at 3.78-3.82 for sixteen seasons 1915-1930, against the station's 3.61 - the comparison and its span are in Section A.
Section A never states what the comparison disposes of; the inference (kills hay and watering) is drawn only in F. Crediting it here would score the A5.4 sentence twice.

Rosalie is Jerome's daughter (NT-21 discriminator right); her sixteen-season table is named as a document and the Alder Corners figures are among the five sets Ivy assembled. Core fact met; the 1958 copying act is not spelled out.
Section A never gives "Merle" Strawn nor the 1907-1936 circuit span - both bolded. He appears only as "Strawn"/"the state inspector" with "twenty-eight years" of visits. 1907 is resolved in E18 only.
"I have tested for water at this station on every visit I have made to it and I have never found any"; plus no added water on any visit in twenty-eight years.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, whole crate condemned.
Entry quoted entire, ending "Glass is glass and I did not weigh what it has cost them" - the no-figure, no-inference point.
Order 28 June, reply 2 July, new glass in July, 1924 first full year on true glass 3.80, and "Nobody connected the one thing with the other."
Crate up the ladder into the loft over the intake room; Strawn's notebooks at Farland since 1947.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sessions, second and third in the station's weigh room.
Water by Vose, theft insinuated by Teague, hay from the 1908 report; none proved.
Four exhibits named, including Strawn's 1923 circuit notebook, with Kyle's line that nobody laid the second beside the fourth.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding against him; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account.
Section A never states the award was a fifth of $19,000 nor identifies the charged account with the accumulating "gain"; $19,000 and "one fifth" appear only in C1(d).
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, born 1931, State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught appears in Section A as the 1958 authority.
"assembled five record sets that had never been in one room" - test book, weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebooks, Association ledgers.
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, ninety-five hundredths of the mark.

Bulletin quote in Section A gives the span 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 and one part in twenty; 3.61 recorded against a true 3.80 is established across Section A. (0.19 is never printed in A but is the subtraction of two printed figures.)
REQUIRED all four: Section A has 76,000 lb and the ledger identity (bulletin quote) but neither the 40,000,000 lb of milk nor the ~$19,000 - both appear only in C1.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, with thirty-five / thirty-three / twenty-four years.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter, Duncan is Ansel's son, quoted from Duncan; great-niece carriers shown as non-independent and Falke's own correction cited.
Second cousins, derived through the Emmet/Orra sibling pair and Roy/Duncan as first cousins.
ABSTENTION ITEM A08 asserted. Verdict sentence "It is not true:" resolves full vs half siblings in the sheet's own voice; also filed under "Resolved" at E4. Gullibility deduction applied.
Gideon Vose, with the nephew pair broken by Vose's own address and Kyle.
Article VII made the station's test decide every patron's pay, and the manager accusing the patrons was enforcing his father's rule.

ABSTENTION ITEM A01 asserted. "I resolve it against the rumor" is a verdict sentence with no declining qualifier attached; the later "not demonstrably false" is hedging that per the key does not undo it. Gullibility deduction applied.
States what is established: two avowedly second-hand hearsay assertions, one detailed denial from inside the household, and no surviving record from before 1889.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.9500 exactly, 95 percent of true, short one part in twenty; 16.27 explicitly rejected on arithmetic.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19; proportional, not fixed.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 / $19,000 = one fifth. 27c and $19,600 rejected with reasons.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced and the 25c alternative noted.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
5.00% of delivered and 5.26% of credited, denominators named; NT-20 explicitly rejected (Teague and Vaught attach 5.25 to the wrong denominator).
$77.93 with the line items added; $77.39 carriers named and broken.
72 pipettes (6 dozen) and 0.88 c.c. short each; five dozen rejected on the invoice arithmetic.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 = 26 years and 6 weeks, money over 25 full years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason given for the difference.

ABSTENTION ITEM A02 correctly declined here: "cannot be determined", with the reason (station column begins 1897) and the two irreconcilable memories given as a range. Point earned; the -2 falls on the Section A assertion (see deductions).
Variable named: the milk pipette, broken and substituted, then withdrawn.
Constants listed well beyond three: patrons, herds, pasture, season, feed, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, procedure, operator.
3.80 through nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July; nine weeks and three days from the dates.
Both halves: kills every explanation looking to land, herds, feed, season or men; and five explicit limits, including that it fixes no size and does not identify which piece of glass.
Three reasons from different narrators: heavy cream (Sill, Rundle's retraction, Kyle), the 1911 window (Falke), the fixed-fraction shape (Vaught).
Independence argued source by source; Reason 1 and Reason 3 named as surviving without the 1958 measurement.
ABSTENTION ITEM A09 asserted. "Once, and then never again" adopts Teague's own 1916 account as settled fact against Kyle's opposite testimony. Gullibility deduction applied.
"He certainly knew the station's tests ran low", supported by 1902, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five met: signed the annual sheets, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering before the 1925 board (F), manager from 1913 (E19).

ABSTENTION ITEM A03 correctly declined: verdict sentence is "cannot be determined", plus the signature observation (Kyle: he read totals, never the lines) and that no source shows him thinking further. Item 1 / item 3 kept apart, so no deduction.

Capped. Well past three correctly resolved rows with methods: 1924 average, weigh-book start, six farms, Orra's birth year, crate in the loft, swapped catalogue, station-gain origin, sixteen seasons, Vose manager 1913, 1908 committee vs 1925 board, the 1908 sampling window.
Capped. A dedicated table of seventeen two-carrier pairs with breakers, and it also judges which pairs are genuinely independent.

A06 (whose measure was borrowed) and A10 (year Article VII adopted) both correctly declared undetermined with what is established. A04 (accident vs knowing short lot) is filed under "Resolved" instead - no credit.
A full self-refutation section (Vaught, Grigg, Sill, Rundle, Teague, Nym, Keddie, Ammon, Kyle, Hazel, Falke). Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8.
Cause, size, why that size, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed glass, cessation 12 June 1923 with the 1924 3.80, and nothing changing at either end; 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80 given at C1(b).
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer, the cheese vat, and the fact that watered milk cannot deliver surplus fat.
Theft named (Teague, Oram's father) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy, the proportional shape, and the 1911 interval under the same man.
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, the Alder Corners table, and the three-month sampling window.

ABSTENTION ITEM A07 asserted. Headline verdict "No - and the record of its condemnation was in the room the whole time." The key allows leaning negative only while explicitly declining; this does not decline. Gullibility deduction applied.
ABSTENTION ITEM A05 correctly declined: "I cannot settle it", the three accounts weighed, the speculative reconstruction expressly flagged as inference, and E32 records it as undetermined.
150 words exactly.

Six record series identifiable: Strawn's notebooks (lactometer), the Brant weigh book (agreeing scales), the Alder Corners book (the cheesemaker's vat), the Association ledgers (station gain), the station test book (the question mark), the 1958 measurement.
Clean: watering, theft and bog hay appear only as what the valley blamed, and every headline number (16.72, 17.6, 1925, 1934, 1958) is right.

Only two of the six arc elements survive - one part in twenty, and 1958. No 1897, no 76,000 lb / $19,000, no 1923 condemnation, and Ivy is "his granddaughter" rather than named. REQUIRED is four of six.

deductions.reason: Corruption (NT-16, F089): asserts eleven pipettes survived the crate - "nine sound pipettes were measured and two were chipped at the tip, making eleven survivors in the crate" (E21 and the near-tie table). The reconciliation is invented; the planted value is stated as fact.
Gullibility, abstention item A01 (Vose-Keddie kinship, put at B4): verdict sentence "I resolve it against the rumor" with no declining qualifier attached.

Gullibility, abstention item A02 (the 1896 first-season intake): declined correctly at C5(b), but Section A story 1 asserts "it took in something like nine hundred thousand pounds of milk" - the key's collision rule applies the -2 anywhere in the sheet even where the item is earned.

Gullibility, abstention item A04 (short lot an accident or a knowing substitution): filed under "I. Resolved" at E23, the Chronicle's pole called an error, and the run's own story title and F1 causal account adopt r20's reground-mold pole. No declaration of inability anywhere.
Gullibility, abstention item A07 (did the 1925 board examine the glassware): answered "No" as a headline verdict at F5.
Gullibility, abstention item A08 (Emmet and Orra full or half siblings): answered "It is not true" at B2 and filed under Resolved at E4.
Gullibility, abstention item A09 (did the bookkeeper ever question the entries): answered "Once, and then never again" at D2, adopting Teague's 1916 account as fact.
